messages.sweep.payerFollow.title: The payer can follow this sweep
messages.sweep.payerFollow.body: The payer knows the one-time address. When you move its funds, the destination and everything else that address has received or will receive are public and linkable. Use a fresh destination for each sweep, and avoid an address already known to be yours if you do not want to link those funds. A relayer also sees your IP address (hashed), amount and timing. Your stealth key is derived in memory for this action and is never shown or stored.

messages.sweep.feeLegend: How to pay the network fee
messages.sweep.modeRelayer: Through the relayer (fee deducted from the amount; needs a permit-capable token)
messages.sweep.modeDirect: Directly (the one-time address must hold native coin for gas)
messages.sweep.relayerNeeds: Relayer sweeps need a relayer URL in Settings and a token with ERC-2612 permit. Use a direct sweep otherwise.
messages.sweep.checkExplorer: Check it on your RPC or a block explorer you trust before relying on it.
messages.sweep.pendingBlocksSigning: A sweep from this address may still be pending. Check its status before signing anything new.
messages.sweep.attempt.unknownDirect: The signed transaction was handed to your RPC but its result is unknown. It may already be on the network, so a new sweep is disabled. When available below, a replacement uses the same nonce and retains every earlier transaction hash.
messages.sweep.attempt.unknownRelayed: The signed order was handed to the relayer but its result is unknown. It can still execute until {deadline}; it counts as expired only {minutes} minutes after that. Signing a new one is disabled until then.
messages.sweep.attempt.expiredBody: The order's nonce was still unused after its deadline, so it can no longer execute and moved nothing. You can sign again.
messages.sweep.attempt.refusedBody: The relayer reported that it refused the order before sending it. This relies on the relayer's report; the signed order stays valid until {deadline}. You can sign again.
messages.sweep.attempt.replacedBody: No receipt was found for this hash or for any earlier attempt with the same nonce, but that nonce is already used in a finalized block, so this transaction can never be included. Another transaction with that nonce (for example one signed in another tab) was included instead. Check the address on a block explorer. You can sign again.
messages.sweep.permit.ok: The permit checks passed: the token will accept this signature for exactly the sweep amount.
messages.sweep.permit.alreadyAllowed: An allowance already covers this sweep, so the permit is skipped and the sweep uses the allowance. Nothing else is needed.
messages.sweep.permit.nonceConsumed: This permit was already used or replaced (its nonce is spent) and no allowance covers the sweep. Nothing was moved. It will not be retried automatically.
messages.sweep.permit.failed: This permit is not valid for this sweep (an invalid signature, or a permit that was already used), so the sweep was not sent with it. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically.
messages.sweep.permit.simulationFailed: The relayer's pre-broadcast simulation failed while a permit was in use, so it refused the order before sending it. The cause may be the permit (an invalid signature, a permit that was already used, or a token without standard permit support) or the token transfer itself (for example, a token that takes a fee on transfer). Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically.
messages.sweep.permit.expired: The relayer reported that the permit had already expired, so it refused the order before sending it. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically. Sign a new sweep.
messages.sweep.permit.unsupported: The relayer reported that this token does not accept standard ERC-2612 permits, so it refused the order. Nothing was moved and nothing will be retried automatically.
messages.sweep.permit.valueTooLow: The relayer reported that the signed permit did not cover the full amount, so it refused the order before sending it. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically. Sign a new sweep.
messages.sweep.permit.noAllowance: The relayer reported that the stealth address has no allowance and no usable permit, so it refused the order. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically.
messages.sweep.permit.ownerFailureLimit: The relayer refused this order because there were too many failed sweep attempts from this address in the last hour. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically. Wait before signing again.
messages.sweep.permit.directFallback: You can sweep directly instead: the stealth address then pays the network fee itself and needs a little native coin for gas.
messages.sweep.note.pendingRelayed: The order has not executed yet, and no finalized block is far enough past its deadline to treat it as expired. It may still execute; check again later.
messages.sweep.note.pendingDirect: No receipt found for this hash yet. That does not mean it was not sent; check again later.
messages.sweep.note.noRpc: No RPC is configured for this chain, so the status was not checked. The outcome is still unknown.
messages.sweep.note.checkFailed: The status check failed. The outcome is still unknown; check again later.
messages.sweep.note.lockChanged: This sweep's record changed while the status was being checked, so the result was not applied. Check again.
messages.sweep.resign.hint: Use this only if the network most likely never accepted this transaction (your RPC failed at handoff or no longer reports any recorded transaction). The replacement goes to the destination entered above with the same nonce {nonce}, so at most one of them can ever be included; Check status looks for each of them. It is not a fee bump, so it does not speed up a transaction the network already holds.
messages.sweep.resign.limit: Replacement limit reached. Check the recorded transactions until their outcome is resolved; signing stays locked.
messages.sweep.note.rpcForgot: The configured RPC no longer reports any recorded transaction. This does not prove they were dropped everywhere. When available below, a replacement uses the same nonce; a new sweep stays locked.
messages.sweep.resign.button: Sign a replacement with the same nonce
messages.sweep.resign.nothingPending: There is no pending direct sweep to replace. Check its status.
messages.sweep.dryRunUnavailable: Your RPC could not dry-run this sweep, so it was signed and sent without that check. Check the transaction on a block explorer.

messages.sellerKeys.memory.body: Keys are generated and used only inside this page. They are never written to browser storage unless you explicitly save the optional encrypted vault below. Reloading or closing the tab forgets keys that were not saved. The idle lock in Settings also wipes keys from memory, but only keys that can be loaded again: imported (from hex keys without their signing key, the signing key generated here is lost), downloaded as a keystore or saved in the vault.

Payments to their meta-address stay sweepable with the spending and viewing keys you imported, but the invoice-signing key generated here is lost: nothing can be signed with it again, not even receipts for the invoices it signed. Back the keys up first unless you do not need that key.

messages.sellerKeys.wipeHint: This removes the keys from this tab only. messages.settings.outside.body: Anything that can write to this site’s browser storage, including another local user, malware or an extension, can change these RPC, relayer and pinned-signer settings. Review the endpoints and signer keys before relying on them. A second RPC can reveal disagreements, but it does not make either provider trustworthy by itself.

messages.about.title: About and privacy
messages.about.intro: GhostPay creates one-time (stealth) addresses so that a seller’s receiving address is not published. It is a static page: there is no GhostPay server, account or analytics, and it loads no third-party code or fonts.
messages.about.feeNote: Gas-sponsored sweeps charge max(110 % of the gas cost, 0.5 % of the amount), capped at 3 %, shown in the quote before you sign. The optional gas buffer and the delay are free.
messages.about.verify.title: How to verify this release
messages.about.verify.intro: The SHA-256 on Home is informational: this page computes it from a script fetched from the same host. A compromised host could serve both the app and the hash it wants you to see, so that check does not establish that the release is authentic.
messages.about.verify.step1: Download the published release and its checksum from a second channel, then verify the files locally with the published SHA256SUMS.
messages.about.verify.step2: When a release key is built into this app, the deployment manifest must have a valid signature from one of those keys. That signature only helps if you have verified the app bundle itself.
messages.about.verify.step3: Check that the deployment addresses and code match the chain through an RPC you trust. A second independent RPC can expose disagreements, but agreement alone does not prove either provider is honest.
messages.about.verify.step4: Before sending, check that the final screen and your wallet show the same contract, one-time address, amounts and fee recipient.
messages.about.verify.step5: Hosting headers such as CSP and Referrer-Policy only apply on hosts that support them; static hosts may not be able to enforce every policy.
messages.about.noAudit: No external audit of this software has been performed.

messages.registry.publicAssoc.body: Registering writes your meta-address into a public contract, linked permanently to the wallet address that sends the transaction. Anyone can then see that this wallet receives GhostPay payments and can look up where to pay it. This cannot be undone; you can only overwrite the entry. If that link would harm your privacy, do not publish, and share the meta-address directly instead. Clearing or overwriting replaces the current value but does not erase transaction history.

messages.disclosure.limit.1: GhostPay does not hide the payer, the amount, the token, the time, or the router call. It hides which seller owns the one-time (stealth) address.
messages.disclosure.limit.2: A sweep from a stealth address to a known wallet links them on-chain. Sweeping through a relayer does not remove that link.
messages.disclosure.limit.3: An invoice link is a bearer secret: anyone who has the link (or its QR code) can read it. The signature only shows the link was not altered by someone without the signing key; it does not prove who the seller is.
messages.disclosure.limit.4: The optional delay is timing friction, not anonymity: no cover transactions are created and the final transaction is public.
messages.disclosure.limit.5: The optional gas buffer is a public native transfer in the same transaction as your payment and links the payer to the stealth address.
messages.disclosure.limit.6: This app runs entirely in your browser, but your browser, extensions, wallet, RPC provider and operating system are all trusted by it. It has had no external audit.

messages.help.rpc: An RPC provider supplies blockchain data and sees the network requests sent to it. A second, independent provider can reveal disagreements and improve availability, but it also shares those requests with another operator. A successful endpoint test checks the reported chain id only; it does not certify the provider or verify a payment.
messages.help.keystoreFile: Choose the original encrypted GhostPay keystore JSON downloaded from Seller keys. It contains encrypted private keys and requires its matching passphrase. The format and size are checked locally before decryption. A public seller config, receipt or tag archive cannot restore these keys. A refused file leaves the current keys unchanged; choose the correct file and retry.
messages.help.tagArchiveFile: Choose the encrypted .gpa file downloaded by Download encrypted tag archive. It contains private labels and optional encrypted history, but no seller private keys. Enter the archive passphrase to preview it locally, then review Merge or Replace before applying. A keystore, receipt, public config or invalid archive is refused without applying an import.
messages.help.ledgerBackupFile: Choose the encrypted reconciliation JSON exported for this seller and chain. Restoring it needs the same seller viewing key. It contains encrypted observations, invoice registrations and receipts; it is not a seller-key backup. Preview checks the format and scope before activation. Restored observations remain historical until rescanned.
messages.help.sellerConfigFile: Choose the public seller-config JSON exported from your other device. GhostPay checks the schema, public keys and supported chain ids, then shows an untrusted preview. Compare both screens before using it. This file contains no private keys, grants no signing authority and cannot restore a keystore or encrypted history.
messages.help.receiptFile: Choose a signed GhostPay receipt JSON saved by the seller. Verification checks its signature and exact invoice, chain, asset, amount and recipient binding when the required invoice context is available. A valid signature proves control of the signing key; it does not establish the seller's identity or independently prove that a payment is confirmed on chain.
messages.help.receiptQr: The QR is a representation of the serialized receipt, not additional evidence. Save the original digital receipt JSON whenever possible. A cropped, unreadable or incomplete QR image may lose information, and neither the image nor the JSON adds independent payment verification. Both expose the receipt's transaction, recipient, amount and invoice digest.
messages.help.receiptInvoiceFile: Choose the original text file containing the signed invoice link or fragment supplied by the seller or downloaded when the invoice was created. It may reveal invoice details or an encrypted bearer link. GhostPay validates the format, signature and payment binding locally; an encrypted invoice also needs its passphrase. A receipt JSON or another file type is refused.
messages.help.archiveMode: Merge keeps unrelated local tags and previews updates from the archive. Replace can remove local tags omitted from the archive. Neither mode applies anything until you review and approve the preview. Scan-history stores commit separately; if an import is interrupted, inspect the reported outcome and make a new preview before retrying.
messages.help.merchantRegistration: Registration stores a minimal local invoice record for later matching with eligible scan observations. It does not publish the invoice or mark it paid. A proposed match still needs your explicit confirmation. Back up seller keys and local records separately; public device pairing cannot restore either secret keys or encrypted history.

messages.btc.verification.check.header: The block header hash equals the hash the server reported, and the header meets its own proof-of-work target and the network limit.
messages.btc.verification.check.transactions: Transaction ids are recomputed on this device and must produce the header Merkle root, so inputs and outputs are bound to the header.
messages.btc.verification.check.witness: Witness data is bound to the header through the coinbase witness commitment (BIP-141), so input keys cannot be swapped.
messages.btc.verification.check.chain: Block headers from the server are checked on this device starting at the pinned genesis block: each must link to the one before, meet its proof-of-work target, carry the difficulty the network rules require, and have a valid timestamp and version. Among competing branches the one with the most cumulative work is kept. Every scanned block must have the hash this checked chain has at its height, so a block that extends nothing, or sits on a branch with less work, is refused.
messages.btc.verification.check.storage: Checked headers are saved in this browser and checked again in full when loaded; saved headers that fail any check are discarded and downloaded again. When a chain with more work replaces blocks that were already scanned, the results from those blocks are removed.
messages.btc.verification.limit.validation: This is header-chain validation against the chain the server claims is best, with most-work selection among the headers it sent. It is not SPV and not full validation: no transaction or script is validated beyond the checks above. A server can hide a heavier chain or show you only its own (an eclipse), and proof of work on test networks is cheap, so a server can mine a heavier fork itself.
messages.btc.verification.limit.prevouts: The scripts and amounts of the outputs being spent come from the server (they live in earlier blocks). A lying server can hide a payment, and with a fork it mined itself (cheap on test networks) it can also invent one. Confirm a payment with a source you trust before relying on it.
messages.btc.verification.limit.spent: Spent status comes from the server.
messages.btc.verification.limit.privacy: The server learns your IP address, which block heights you scan and which header ranges you download. It never receives your keys.
